title: Edge-relay and backend fences with no capability name
why: Two rows that name no capability because neither is a feature — both inventory cells read «no capability named on the inventory row» and await signature on exactly that point. `S-628` is pure dispatch on the Beget relay: three case arms that hand straight to one shared include, whose opening line states plainly that authentication and Client authority are checked by Maya. What narrow checking exists lives in that include, not in the dispatch — it maps each permitted action to one fixed backend route, rejects any payload key outside that action's list, and refuses a forwarded channel header containing CR or LF, answering 400 before anything leaves Beget. `S-634` is a small Maya-local backend command that persists a visit-mood flag; per its own docstring it carries no phone authority and no CRM sync, and any failure returns 409 `preference_request_rejected`. Authority stays server-side in Maya — these two are the transport in front of it and one narrow sink behind it, not the place where a decision is made.
disappear: Nothing. Both rows carry the K15 "retired as UI" condition, but neither has any UI to retire — the successor cell on each reads "server-side fence (no UI successor)".
remain: Both stay as they are. On the relay: the three dispatch cases `cabinet_link_phone` (L371), `native_feedback` (L377) and `notify_prefs` (L382) — the case is `notify_prefs`, not `notify` — each handing off to `maya_client_consent_proxy` in `package5-client-consent-proxy.php`. On the backend: `set_visit_mood_handler`, with a single route registration for `/api/set-visit-mood` (L9982). One fix is owed before this group is treated as clean: the comment at L376 («Персональные настройки уведомлений клиента») describes the notify_prefs case but sits directly above `case 'native_feedback'`, and must be moved down to L381.
risk: LOW — with its two defects named rather than left invisible. Both are wrong text, not wrong behaviour. First, the comment at L376 describes notify_prefs but sits above the feedback case, so a future edit to the consent block guided by it lands on the wrong arm; it is the only actionable item in the group and a bare "LOW" hid it. Second, the proposed-owner cell going to signature names `notify`, a case that does not exist — it must read `notify_prefs`, or an editor searching for it will not find the arm. Nothing here is a parity gap. The relay file is pinned to the deployed bytes by a 2026-09-08 read of the live copy (2413 lines, every byte identical apart from the substituted PARTNER_TOKEN and COMPANY_ID), and the include is pinned by the same certified edge manifest, whose recorded post-deploy hash `267383a9…` is byte-identical to the copy under `maya-saas-backend/deploy/vps/` that the committed architecture tests read. One residual remains, and it is too narrow to move the level: those tests assert the include's text rather than exercise it, and the include has had no independent live re-read since that deploy landed.
user_impact: No user notices anything — not the owner, not a staff member, not a client. Both rows are server-side plumbing with no UI and no primary-nav entry (`primaryNav: false` on both), and the group is an attribution only: nothing is replaced, nothing is retired, no code moves, so the 101→5 nav collapse does not touch it. S-634 is a single POST route (`/api/set-visit-mood`, registered once at `webhook_server.py` L9982) that persists a red/blue mood flag on a visit; the screens that write that flag are different rows (S-439 `vmood_*` pills in bot.py, S-648 `mayaClientPreferenceCall` in app.html, S-629 the relay's own `set_visit_mood` arm), and this one only stores what they send. S-628 is three forwarding `case` arms — `cabinet_link_phone` L371, `native_feedback` L377, `notify_prefs` L382 — each of which is `require_once` + `maya_client_consent_proxy(...)` + `break`. Provenance caveat the row carries and the claim must not drop: those are line numbers in `maya-saas-backend/test/fixtures/beget/api-proxy.sanitized.php`, a sanitized FIXTURE. The live api-proxy.php is absent from the worktree (`сайт и приложение/pwa-assets/tg-auth/` holds only .htaccess variants, INSTRUCTION-DEPLOY.md, requirements.txt and a .sql file), so the deployed dispatcher was never read. "No user notices anything" therefore holds because signing an owner name changes no code at all, not because the live relay was inspected and found to have no UI.
security_impact: Direction is NONE, and that survives: no check is removed, re-parented ahead of a server gate, or added; neither fence was ever a client-side check; signing this group is an attribution only. But two credits are misassigned and two conditions are papered over. (1) The three S-628 arms decide and check NOTHING — each is `require_once` + `maya_client_consent_proxy($action, $input, $TG_CONFIG)` + `break`. The shape-check lives in the callee, `maya-saas-backend/deploy/vps/package5-client-consent-proxy.php`: route table L13, allowed-key diff L15 (`array_diff` → 400 `invalid_client_command`), CRLF in a forwarded `X-Telegram-InitData`/`Authorization` L23 (also surfaced as 400 `invalid_client_command`, same wire body). That file is a separate inventory row (S-623), so the fence must not be booked to S-628. Because each arm passes its own literal action, the unknown-action branch at L13 is unreachable from them; the key-set diff is the only check that can fire. The include header — "A18 transport only. Authentication and Client authority are checked by Maya" — is quoted correctly. (2) S-634 does fail closed in real, verified code: key-set diff at `webhook_server.py` L9084 rejects any unexpected key; `channel_proof` (`legacy_client_command_bridge.py` L13-27) raises `verified_channel_required` at L26 when no init-data header, `Bearer`, or body `auth_data` is present — note `maya_token` can never reach it on this route, it is not in the allowed key set; the bare `except` turns every failure into 409 `preference_request_rejected` with `client_link_required: true`; and the tenant is bound server-side from `config.YCLIENTS_COMPANY_ID` in `legacy_client_preferences_bridge.command` (L10, L17), never from the request body. This is a running code fence, not one of the thirteen-of-twenty-one rules that hold only vacuously, and no frozen limitation is touched: STEP_UP unreachable, Gate 10 measured-not-enforced, role-gated approval (not separation-of-duties) and GAP-ATTENDANCE-CONFIRM are all unaffected by these two rows. The two conditions the attribution must carry: (a) the stated parity requirement, "the fence fires independently of any UI, proved by test," is currently UNSATISFIABLE for S-628 — the live api-proxy.php is absent from the worktree, and a test against the sanitized fixture proves a property of the fixture, not of the deployed dispatcher; it is satisfiable today only for S-634; (b) the row carries a live editing trap the dossier's own rationale says to fix — the comment at fixture L376 ("Персональные настройки уведомлений клиента") describes `notify_prefs` but sits above `case 'native_feedback'` after the R08 overlay, so a future consent-block edit trusting the comment lands on the wrong fence arm. Neither is a loosening today; both are why "both fences stay exactly as they are" is asserted with more certainty than the evidence supports.
